name: 001_help_short.sh
expected: exits 0 and writes a help message to standard output
manpage_quote: Display a short help message to the standard output and exit.

name: 002_help_long.sh
expected: exits 0 and writes a help message to standard output
manpage_quote: -h, --help

name: 003_version_string.sh
expected: exits 0 and output contains a version string
manpage_quote: Print the sudo version string

name: 004_exit_status_propagation.sh
exercises: exit-status propagation from the run command
expected: sudo exits with the command's exit status 7
manpage_quote:
the exit status from sudo will be
     the exit status of the program that was executed

name: 005_exit_status_success.sh
exercises: exit-status propagation for a successful command
expected: sudo exits 0 when the command exits 0
manpage_quote:
the exit status from sudo will be
     the exit status of the program that was executed

name: 006_command_stdout.sh
exercises: sudo runs the given command and relays its stdout
expected: command stdout 'hello_sudo' reaches the caller
manpage_quote:
execute a command as the superuser or
     another user

name: 007_user_name_identity.sh
expected: id -un prints the target user daemon
manpage_quote: Run the command as a user other than the default target user

name: 008_user_numeric_uid.sh
expected: id -u prints 0 for '#0'
manpage_quote:
The user may be either a user name or a numeric
             user-ID (UID) prefixed with the ‘#’ character (e.g., ‘#0’ for UID
             0).

name: 009_group_name.sh
expected: id -gn prints the target group daemon
manpage_quote: Run the command with the primary group set to group

name: 010_group_numeric_gid.sh
expected: id -g prints 0 for '#0'
manpage_quote:
a
             numeric group-ID (GID) prefixed with the ‘#’ character (e.g.,
             ‘#0’ for GID 0)

name: 011_group_without_user_runs_as_invoking.sh
expected: id -un stays root (the invoking user)
manpage_quote:
If no -u
             option is specified, the command will be run as the invoking
             user.

name: 012_chdir_directory.sh
expected: pwd reports the requested directory
manpage_quote:
Run the command in the specified directory instead of the current
             working directory.

name: 013_end_of_options.sh
expected: token after -- is passed to the command, not sudo
manpage_quote:
The -- is used to delimit the end of the sudo options.
             Subsequent options are passed to the command.

name: 014_env_assignment.sh
exercises: VAR=value environment assignment passed as an option
expected: command sees MYVAR=set_via_sudo
manpage_quote:
Environment variables to be set for the command may also be passed as
     options to sudo in the form VAR=value

name: 015_preserve_env_all.sh
expected: arbitrary parent var survives into the command env
manpage_quote:
Indicates to the security policy that the user wishes to preserve
             their existing environment variables.

name: 016_preserve_env_list.sh
exercises: --preserve-env=list adds named vars to preserved set
expected: named var PRESERVE_ONE survives into the command env
manpage_quote:
Indicates to the security policy that the user wishes to add the
             comma-separated list of environment variables to those preserved
             from the user's environment.

name: 017_set_home.sh
exercises: -H / --set-home sets HOME to target user's home
expected: HOME equals root's passwd-database home directory
manpage_quote:
Set to the home directory of the target user when the -i
                      or -H options are specified

name: 018_shell_option_command.sh
exercises: -s / --shell runs a specified command via the shell
expected: command output 'shell_ran' produced through the shell
manpage_quote:
If a command is specified, it is passed to the
             shell as a simple command using the -c option.

name: 019_login_shell_command.sh
exercises: -i / --login runs a specified command via login shell
expected: command output 'login_ran' produced through the login shell
manpage_quote:
If a command is specified, it is passed to the shell
             as a simple command using the -c option.

name: 020_login_sets_home.sh
stderr: expected sudo -i to run, exited 2: %s: 1: printf: usage: printf format [arg ...]
exercises: -i sets HOME to the target user's home directory
expected: HOME equals root's passwd-database home directory
manpage_quote:
Set to the home directory of the target user when the -i
                      or -H options are specified

name: 021_login_sets_logname.sh
stderr: expected sudo -i -u daemon to run, exited 1:
exercises: -i sets LOGNAME to the target user's login name
expected: LOGNAME equals daemon under -i -u daemon
manpage_quote:
Set to the login name of the target user when the -i
                      option is specified

name: 022_sudo_user_env.sh
exercises: SUDO_USER set to the invoking user's login name
expected: command sees SUDO_USER=root (the invoking user)
manpage_quote: Set to the login name of the user who invoked sudo.

name: 023_sudo_command_env.sh
stderr: expected SUDO_COMMAND to include the run command path, got 'sh -c printf %s "${SUDO_COMMAND:-MISSING}"'
exercises: SUDO_COMMAND set to the command run by sudo
expected: SUDO_COMMAND names the run command path
manpage_quote: Set to the command run by sudo, including any args.

name: 024_list_privileges.sh
expected: exits 0 for a permitted, authenticated user
manpage_quote:
If no command is specified, list the privileges for the invoking
             user

name: 025_unknown_user_error.sh
exercises: -u with a nonexistent target user (documented error)
expected: sudo exits nonzero (cannot execute / config problem)
manpage_quote:
If there is an authentication failure, a configuration/permission
     problem, or if the given command cannot be executed, sudo exits with a
     value of 1.

name: 026_close_from_too_small_error.sh
exercises: -C with a value less than three (documented error)
expected: sudo exits nonzero
manpage_quote: Values less than three are not permitted.

name: 027_duplicate_user_option_error.sh
stderr: expected duplicate -u to fail, but sudo exited 0
expected: sudo exits nonzero
manpage_quote:
Options that take a value may only be specified once unless otherwise
     indicated in the description.

name: 028_preserve_env_invalid_name_error.sh
expected: sudo exits nonzero (invalid environment variable name)
manpage_quote:
One or more environment variable names specified via the -E option
           contained an equal sign (‘=’).

name: 029_remove_timestamp_with_command_error.sh
stderr: expected -K with a command to fail, but sudo exited 0
expected: sudo exits nonzero
manpage_quote:
It is
             not possible to use the -K option in conjunction with a command
             or other option.
